description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the 38-hour week formula. Includes salary sacrifice car, tax, super, and minimum wage details.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, annual gross is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard 38-hour week, annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. This assumes no overtime, penalty rates, or salary sacrifice. Use our [the timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. The National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05 per hour (including loading). Our [the timesheet](/) has a checkbox to add casual loading automatically.

faqs.q: Can I salary sacrifice a car with my employer?
faqs.a: Yes, many employers offer salary sacrifice arrangements for a car, where you forego part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for the vehicle. This reduces your taxable income and can lower your tax bill. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more on salary packaging.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay, Including Salary Sacrifice Car Options

Understanding your annual pay from an hourly rate is essential whether you're negotiating a salary, budgeting, or planning a salary sacrifice car arrangement. This guide explains the conversion formula, the role of the 38-hour week, and how tax and super affect your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay is calculated as:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a standard 38-hour week, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman for full-time employment. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. For example, a $30 per hour rate gives:

$30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year (before tax and super).

Your fortnightly pay is roughly weekly pay × 2. For $30/hour, weekly pay is $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280 before deductions.

### Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. Award rates often exceed the minimum; check your industry award via our [pay guides](/blog). The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week nationally (May 2026), but state averages differ—see our [reference tables](/data) for breakdowns.

### Superannuation and Salary Sacrifice

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross pay at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. For a $30/hour worker, annual super is $59,280 × 12% = $7,113.60, added to your pay package.

A **salary sacrifice car** arrangement lets you use pre-tax income to pay for a vehicle, reducing your taxable income. For example, sacrificing $10,000 per year lowers your assessable income, potentially saving tax at your marginal rate. However, it also reduces your super guarantee base (since super is calculated on ordinary earnings after sacrifice). Always consult a tax professional. Learn more on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Resident tax for 2026–27: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are unconfirmed).

For a $59,280 annual gross, tax is roughly:
- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($4,020)
- 30% on $14,280 ($4,284)
Total tax ≈ $8,304, plus Medicare $1,185.60, leaving about $49,790.40 take-home (excluding super). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a precise estimate.

### Using Our Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It calculates annual gross, fortnightly pay, tax, Medicare, and super. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading—use the checkbox instead.

### Key Distinctions

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44/hour (adult, non-casual).
- **Award rates**: Vary by industry; check [pay guides](/blog).
- **Casual loading**: 25% on top of base rate.
- **Super**: 12% paid on top, not deducted from your pay.
- **Salary sacrifice**: Reduces taxable income; a salary sacrifice car is a common option.

Remember, annual pay here is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed calculations, explore our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) pages.
